title: Can Sound Really Shatter Glass?
description:
A voice can break a glass—but only if frequency, loudness and the glass all line up.

A sustained sound near the glass’s natural frequency can drive resonance; if vibration stress exceeds the material’s strength, cracks can grow and the glass can fail.

The effect requires a suitable thin glass, accurate pitch and high sound level; it is not easy with ordinary speech.

The glass vibrates before it breaks, and laser or high-speed measurements can reveal the growing amplitude.
